dedupe_keys.name: where flood risk outruns insurance evidence from two decades of expanding combined risk hotspots across the contiguous united states

description: University of Alabama researchers publish a combined-risk-hotspot dataset for the contiguous United States. Zenodo supplies an archive free under CC BY 4.0, with geospatial layers, tabular inputs and Python notebooks. It joins 2000–2023 land-cover change, FEMA flood exposure, Census demographics, social vulnerability and National Flood Insurance Program loss records. Focused analyses cover Baton Rouge, Houston, Jacksonville, Orlando and Tampa. These layers can inform flood-exposure, adaptation and disaster-financing simulations. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this combined release. Coverage is the national synthesis and five named metros, not independently measured uninsured loss for every property. A limitation is that hotspots depend on thresholds and source vintages; the phrase underinsurance is an analytical conclusion, not a directly observed asset attribute. Component licences and geographic resolution need checking inside the archive. No file was downloaded or hotspot ranking reproduced.
